content.title: WHAT HAPPENS TO YOUR BODY WHEN YOU {{ALWAYS EAT FRUIT LAST}}
facts: **Fruit after a big meal** – can sit on top of heavier food and ferment before it fully digests, which is why you sometimes feel bloated after a 'healthy' dessert.
**Herbal tea all evening** – many blends are mildly diuretic, so a nightly pot right before bed can wake you up for bathroom trips more than plain water would.
**Walking barefoot on hard floors** – feels natural, but long stretches on tile or concrete without support can quietly strain your arches and lower back over months.
**Deep stretching cold** – stretching muscles before they're warm can overextend fibers instead of loosening them, raising the odds of a small strain.
**Sleeping with a phone alarm nearby** – the habit of checking the time when you wake at night trains your brain to fully wake up instead of drifting back to sleep.
**Rinsing your mouth right after eating** – doing it immediately, especially after acidic food, can rub softened enamel before saliva has time to re-harden it.
**Long weekend lie-ins** – sleeping 2-3 hours past your normal wake time shifts your body clock enough that Monday morning can feel like mild jet lag.

content.caption:
A few of these are worth slowing down on. Fruit is packed with fiber and vitamins, but when it's eaten right on top of a heavy meal, the sugars can get trapped behind slower-digesting food and start to ferment in the gut, which is where that post-meal bloat comes from — eating it on its own or before the meal instead usually solves it. Herbal tea feels like the gentlest evening ritual there is, but certain common blends (like dandelion or hibiscus-based ones) gently push your kidneys to release more fluid, so a big mug right before lights-out can work against the deep sleep you're trying to protect. And weekend lie-ins are so tempting after a tiring week, but pushing your wake time back by a couple hours resets your internal clock's sense of 'morning,' so you end up paying it back with grogginess on Monday. Everyone's body responds a little differently, so notice what actually happens to yours.
